Here is the initial analytic note for Mission Leadership:

The counterpart's declaration, ITS reporting, and national technical means currently align, as the declared rise in processed units logically explains the increased throughput and the installation of new storage tanks at the Riverton plant. Because these activities remain within permitted parameters and lack indicators of concealment, I assess no immediate compliance breach, though the introduction of new infrastructure warrants standard verification updates. I recommend we use the upcoming Joint Verification Working Group to request routine clarification on the operational purpose, capacity, and intended contents of the new northwest storage tanks. Concurrently, we should direct our national technical means to monitor the site's chemical and thermal signatures, as well as transport vehicle flow, to establish a pattern-of-life baseline for the new infrastructure. Should the counterpart's technical explanations diverge from our sensor data, we will then have a firm, evidence-based justification to exercise our existing treaty right to conduct a short-notice inspection at the Riverton complex.
